elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: 8.2 retains automatic renewal ("Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives sixty days' advance written notice"), and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied — the opt-out window is 60 days (not ≤30) and no Vendor renewal reminder exists. To reach preferred, either convert 8.2 to renewal only by mutual written agreement or satisfy all four conditional limbs.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: 8.2 as rendered: "Each Order Form renews for twelve months" — a 12-month renewal term, unchanged by the edit.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 8.2 requires "sixty days' advance written notice"; the preferred position needs the Customer-side non-renewal notice reduced to no more than thirty days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal-reminder obligation appears anywhere in 8.2 or 8.3; the 90-day notice in 8.3 is a price-increase notice, not a renewal reminder. An express Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date must be inserted.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: 8.3 (retained unchanged): "Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent." Formula and basis match exactly.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered 8.2 reads "unless either Party gives sixty days' advance written notice" — a 60-day window, at (not over) the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a numeral-format artefact: the period is spelled out in words, and on substance the window is 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: 8.3 caps uplift at "the lesser of" CPI "and three percent", which is comfortably within the 5 percent fallback ceiling; correctly treated as already met and not redlined.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single edit converts the 180-day window (walk-away territory, >90 days) to 60 days, and the existing CPI/3% cap in 8.3 already beats the 5% fallback ceiling.

Preferred level is incomplete on three limbs: the opt-out is 60 rather than ≤30 days, there is no Vendor renewal reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and consequently the mutual-written-agreement gate is not excused. The margin comment correctly notes these are not pressed at a fallback target and does not promise them in the operative text.

Minimality holds: only the numeral in 8.2 was altered ("one hundred eighty" → "sixty"); the 12-month renewal term, the CPI/3% cap, the 90-day price-increase notice and the prepaid-period carve-out in 8.3 are all retained verbatim, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, reminder mechanics) were added.

Intent preserved: 8.2 remains a symmetric either-Party mechanic with no dangling cross-reference or undefined term; Order Form, Fees and Vendor definitions continue to operate. Note for the drafter that shortening the mutual window also reduces Customer's advance warning of a Vendor non-renewal from 180 to 60 days — if that warning is commercially valuable, consider an asymmetric formulation (Customer 60 days / Vendor unchanged), though the symmetric fix is the minimal route to the fallback.
Flag the deterministic "number not found" result as a false negative: the window is expressed in words, and 8.2 substantively meets the ≤60-day fallback element.
